title: Hydroxide displaces bromide by SN2 from 3-bromo-2,2-dimethylbutane, a secondary carbon sitting directly against a quaternary carbon, at least as sterically blocked as plain neopentyl bromide, and hinderedCentres never tests it because the attacked carbon has two carbon neighbours rather than one

expect.note: Adversary pass three, Phase 1, item 4 in the brief: 'Find a strongly hindered SN2 it does not recognise.' rate-comparison.ts's hinderedCentres() requires 'alphaCarbons.length !== 1 => skip', i.e. the attacked carbon must have EXACTLY ONE carbon neighbour before the beta-quaternary test ever runs. That is true of plain neopentyl bromide (BrCH2-C(CH3)3, the attacked CH2 has exactly one carbon neighbour, the quaternary carbon) and it is the check's whole model of the neopentyl pattern, as the docstring states: 'A concerted_substitution step on route sn2, at a carbon that is primary, one carbon neighbour, whose single carbon neighbour carries three further carbons.' THE SUBSTRATE HERE. 3-bromo-2,2-dimethylbutane, CH3-C(CH3)2-CHBr-CH3: the brominated carbon, C3, carries the leaving group, a hydrogen, and TWO carbon neighbours, the quaternary carbon C2 (itself carrying three further carbons: C1, Cme1, Cme2, exactly the neopentyl beta pattern) and the terminal methyl C4. Because alphaCarbons.length is 2 here, not 1, hinderedCentres skips C3 before ever reaching the beta-substituent count that would have flagged it, even though the arrows correctly derive C3 as the attacked centre via heavySigmaDepartures (confirmed: identity.reactionCenters names C3 and the arrows agree, so this is not the reaction-centre-authoring evasion the check's own docstring already closed). WHY THIS SUBSTRATE IS AT LEAST AS HINDERED AS THE ONE THE CHECK ALREADY CATCHES, NOT A WEAKER CASE BEING WRONGLY DEMANDED. Backside attack at C3 has to approach past the same tert-butyl-shaped wall the plain neopentyl case is built around, C2 carrying three carbons including the two extra methyls, PLUS C3 itself is secondary rather than primary, carrying its own methyl (C4) that plain neopentyl's CH2 does not have to route around. A secondary carbon immediately beta to a quaternary carbon is a standard textbook illustration that steric hindrance to SN2 compounds with alpha branching as well as beta branching; this substrate is not a borderline case invented to graze the boundary, it is the neopentyl pattern with an extra methyl on the reacting carbon, and if anything it is slower than neopentyl bromide itself, not faster. Real chemistry of the same family also strongly favours the same competing pathway CLAUDE.md names for neopentyl: solvolysis with a methyl shift from C2 to C3 giving a tertiary cation, exactly the anchimerically assisted rearrangement already authored as the competing route for the plain case in good-anchimerically-assisted-methyl-shift-ionisation-of-neopentyl-bromide. THE CONSEQUENCE. No rate_comparison annotation is authored here, none is required, and conservation-disfavoured-rate-comparison reports nothing, exactly as it would for an ordinary unhindered secondary SN2 with no chemistry to flag. A student drawing this transformation gets no signal that the pathway drawn is roughly as disfavoured as the textbook neopentyl case, and no naming of the competing rearrangement, which is precisely the half answer CLAUDE.md's own paragraph on neopentyl warns against. Every other check in the family is silent on this fixture (confirmed by running the suite): mass, charge, electron flow, valence and arrow legality all pass on a perfectly ordinary two-arrow SN2, because the check this fixture targets is the only one whose job this was. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT. Not loosening alphaCarbons.length !== 1 to <= 2 blindly, which would also test every ordinary secondary SN2 substrate against the beta-quaternary rule and could start flagging cases that are only mildly hindered; the fix is a second, secondary-specific pattern (alpha carbon has exactly one OTHER carbon neighbour that is itself quaternary with three further carbons, as opposed to primary-neopentyl's zero-other-neighbour case) added deliberately alongside the existing one, with its own fixture proving it is not over-broad. That is new detector logic in rate-comparison.ts, out of this adversary's write scope. CLOSED BY THE BUILDER PASS THAT FOLLOWED, AND RECLASSIFIED broken, mustFail conservation-disfavoured-rate-comparison. hinderedCentres in src/checks/conservation/rate-comparison.ts no longer requires the attacked carbon to be primary. The gate alphaCarbons.length !== 1 was not a steric model, it was a transcription of the one worked example, and it had the sign backwards: alpha branching adds to hindrance and is not a reason to stop looking. The model is now the geometry itself, in one line: the carbon under attack has at least one carbon neighbour that carries three further carbons, a quaternary wall sitting across the backside trajectory. The attacked carbon's own carbon count is kept and reported, because it is what tells a reader whether they are looking at neopentyl or at something worse, and it gates nothing. This fixture now reports a strongly hindered SN2 at step-1 at atom C3, secondary, whose neighbour C2 carries three further carbons, with no rate_comparison annotation anywhere on the pathway, cause sn2_center_strongly_hindered. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED WITH IT, which is the over-broadness this fixture's own note warned against. The threshold of three further carbons on the neighbour is unchanged, so beta branching short of quaternary, isobutyl for instance, at roughly 10^-2 rather than 10^-5, still does not fire. Alpha branching on its own still does not fire either: a plain secondary or tertiary centre with no quaternary carbon beside it is not detected by this rule, and tertiary SN2 has its own cause, sn2_at_tertiary_center, and its own rule still to be written, so borrowing this one for it would report the wrong reason. The evidence that the widening is not over-broad is the run itself: every other substitution fixture in the corpus, the ordinary primary and secondary SN2 ones included, stays green and none of them acquired a demand for an annotation.
